findings.claim: Stack Overflow 2024 survey (65,000+ devs): only 18.5% highly trust AI tools, 53.6% somewhat trust, ~27.5% little/no trust. 76.1% using or planning to use AI tools. Learning devs trust AI more (70.6%) vs professionals (39.5%).
By 2025, trust in AI accuracy dropped to 29-33% (from 43% in 2024) even as usage rose to 84%, creating a widening adoption-trust paradox.
GitHub Octoverse 2024: 92% of US-based developers using AI coding tools at work.
Harness 2024: 42% of respondents cite lack of trust in AI output as the #1 barrier to automating code review. 60% worry AI introduces technical debt.

Atlassian 2024: 63% of devs report AI provides high-quality review suggestions, but 45% feel AI leads to rubber-stamping culture. Trust increases significantly when AI provides rationale for suggestions.
AI reduces PR creation time by ~58%, but complex AI-generated PRs wait 4.6x longer in review queues. PR review times increased 91% after AI adoption (10,000+ dev telemetry study, 2025).
AI-generated contributions contain ~1.7x more issues than human PRs. Readability issues (unclear naming, nested complexity) are 3x more common in AI-generated code.
Microsoft Research 2024: developers reviewing AI-generated code missed 40% more bugs than when reviewing human code, due to 'veneer of correctness' where perfect syntax masks logical errors.
GitClear 2024-2025 data: 39.9% decrease in refactoring (moved lines) and 8x increase in duplicated code attributed to AI coding assistants.
Six Levels of Autonomous Software Engineering framework (arxiv, March 2024) maps L0 (no automation) through L5 (full autonomy), modeled after SAE self-driving levels.
GitHub Copilot Workspace (April 2024) implements plan-first progressive autonomy: AI generates human-readable plan from issue, human approves plan before agent writes code.

Agent Protocol (2024) defines standardized capability negotiation where AI agents request specific permissions (file system, network, shell) that humans grant temporarily or permanently based on task performance.

Four progressive autonomy rollout patterns identified: Shadow Mode (agreement rate), Review-First (approval velocity), Sandboxed Autonomy (verification success), Permission Escalation (task success streak).
Human-on-the-Loop (HOTL) transition from HITL mediated by trust calibration metrics -- quantifiable data on how often AI suggestions are accepted without modification.
Qodo PR-Agent uses structured 'PR Walkthrough' contract: high-level summary, categorized changes, file-by-file walkthrough with mandatory rationale for every significant hunk.

Modern AI PR contracts follow four-part structure: (1) Executive Summary, (2) Impact Matrix with risk levels, (3) Verification Contract with test results/CI logs, (4) AI-Labeling Convention for different review workflows.

Graphite (2024) pivoted to intent-based PR descriptions: AI explains intent behind changes and potential side effects, separating Intent/Changes/Testing sections. Also uses RAG-grounded fix rationale.
Competence-Reliability-Transparency (CRT) Model (Edmonds Commerce, 2025): measures trust across four dimensions -- Competence, Reliability, Transparency, and Safety.

Agentic TDD framework: humans write tests first, trust is managed by agent's ability to pass pre-defined tests. Trust penalized when agent writes both code and its own tests (unreliable self-validation).
Qodo 2025 survey: 65% of developers feel AI assistants miss relevant context. Most requested improvement (26%) is better architectural reasoning explaining how changes fit the existing codebase.
Teams using autonomous agents report 43% increase in manual code review activity -- developers shifting from 'author' to 'auditor' role.
Snyk 2024: 56.6% of devs believe AI code is more secure than human code, yet 80% of organizations restrict AI use due to security/hallucination fears. 38% concerned about training data security.

Leading 2025 AI review tools (CodeRabbit, Cursor) achieve 42-48% bug detection accuracy, double traditional static analyzers (~20%). Top models correctly classify code correctness only 64-68% of the time.
AI-generated code requires 2x more rework within 30-90 days compared to human code, despite mature teams reporting 80-90% initial acceptance rate for AI suggestions.

UX patterns reducing review fatigue (2024-2025): PR executive summaries with grouped issues, confidence gradients with visual indicators, visual differentiation of AI vs human comments, one-click remediation batching, risk-based file highlighting.

key_insights: Developers are rapidly integrating AI into workflows despite concurrent trust decline (84% usage vs 29% trust by 2025), indicating perceived productivity gains currently outweigh confidence in output quality.

The velocity gained during AI-assisted authoring is neutralized by a severe downstream bottleneck: reviewers face higher cognitive loads, PRs wait 4.6x longer in queues, and reviewers miss 40% more bugs in AI code due to its veneer of syntactic correctness.

Sustainable trust depends less on fix accuracy and more on the system's ability to communicate architectural rationale and intent -- structured verification contracts (plan-first, impact matrices, rationale-driven descriptions) are emerging as the primary trust-building mechanism.
gaps: No longitudinal studies found on how rubber-stamping culture and AI-driven code duplication affect junior engineer skill development over multi-year periods.
Insufficient controlled A/B testing data comparing specific review UI patterns (e.g., confidence gradients vs executive summaries) for their impact on defect detection rates.
No standardized economic model correlating accelerated PR creation velocity with long-term maintenance costs from decreased readability and increased technical debt.
